name: hh-meanrev-micro: double-confirm extreme reversal, vol veto (15m)
rationale: MECHANISM: require TWO independent overextension reads to AGREE — a statistical extreme (bb_z, distance-from-mean) AND a momentum-exhaustion extreme (rsi) — to filter the false-positive fades that single-signal reversion suffers (a low bb_z alone is common on a strong trend day and gets run over). The conjunction is rarer and selects moments where BOTH the price-level and the rate-of-change say the move is spent, better isolating genuine forced-flow overshoot from ordinary trend. The other side is the crowd that piled into the last leg of a fast move. vol_realized is used only as a CAPACITY veto (skip when vol is so high the spread blows out), not as a trigger. Entry: bb_z below a fitted floor AND rsi below a fitted floor simultaneously AND vol_realized below a fitted ceiling. Long-only spot; exit on bb_z reversion. DISCONFIRMER: ablate — if the double-confirm net result is NOT better than the better of the two single signals alone, the conjunction is redundant (the features are collinear at extremes) — prefer the single signal or kill. Second: if the rarer signal fires mostly during the same handful of cascade days, effective-N collapses and the DSR/FDR gate will (correctly) reject it — treat low effective-N as a kill, not a tuning target.
catalyst: simultaneous band and momentum extremes agree on a spent move
